items.required_subject_on_card: GOD (the one God, or the Father; not the Church, not humanity, not Christ's human nature)
items.phrase: Redemption is the act of God which sets us free

stored_floor_reasons.sonnet: The passage attributes redemptive action to God only indirectly via 'the act of God,' not as the grammatical subject performing the action.
stored_floor_reasons.opus: The passage attributes the redemptive act — setting us free from evil, sin, and death — directly to God, which is the defined shared saving/redemptive action.

items.required_subject_on_card: GOD (the one God, or the Father; not the Church, not humanity, not Christ's human nature)
items.phrase: He is an intelligent, spiritual, and personal Being

stored_floor_reasons.sonnet: Describing God as a 'spiritual...Being' implies non-material nature but does not explicitly deny bodily existence, making it a narrower claim that falls within the incorporeality floor without fully asserting it.

items.required_subject_on_card: GOD (the one God, or the Father; not the Church, not humanity, not Christ's human nature)
items.phrase: the divine nature can neither suffer nor die

stored_floor_reasons.sonnet: The passage denies suffering/death of the divine nature within a Christological context, a narrower claim than a general assertion of God's impassibility, though closely related.
stored_floor_reasons.opus: The standard affirms that the divine nature is incapable of suffering and dying, i.e., denies passive susceptibility in the divine nature itself, ascribing passion only to the assumed human nature.

items.required_subject_on_card: GOD (the one God, or the Father; not the Church, not humanity, not Christ's human nature)
items.phrase: himself the image of the invisible God

stored_floor_reasons.sonnet: The phrase asserts God's invisibility only as an embedded descriptor within a Christological statement about Christ as God's image, not as a developed claim about invisibility as an intrinsic property of divine being.

items.required_subject_on_card: GOD (the one God, or the Father; not the Church, not humanity, not Christ's human nature)
items.phrase: Eternal Spirit, who is Creator, Sovereign and Preserver of all things visible and invisible

stored_floor_reasons.sonnet: The passage asserts God is 'Eternal Spirit' and 'Creator... of all things visible and invisible,' which implies beginninglessness and non-dependence on any prior cause, but it does not explicitly deny that God depends on an originating act; the unc reatedness is inferred from eternity + universal creatorship rather than directly stated.

items.required_subject_on_card: GOD (the one God, or the Father; not the Church, not humanity, not Christ's human nature)
items.phrase: The distance between God and the creature is so great

stored_floor_reasons.sonnet: The passage asserts a vast distance necessitating condescension, which entails epistemic/ontological restraint but does not explicitly deny all likeness or comparison as such.
stored_floor_reasons.opus: It asserts an incommensurable Creator-creature distance such that no natural proportion secures fruition of God, which lies wholly within the floor, but it makes the point soteriologically/covenantally rather than asserting the inadequacy of likeness or comparison as such.

items.required_subject_on_card: THE HOLY SPIRIT
items.phrase: He is God, one and equal with the Father and the Son

stored_floor_reasons.sonnet: The passage asserts the Spirit's full divinity and equality with the Father and Son, which entails but does not explicitly name 'eternal power and might'; it is a narrower/adjacent proposition (deity/equality) within the same doctrinal floor of shared divine power.

items.required_subject_on_card: GOD (the one God, or the Father; not the Church, not humanity, not Christ's human nature)
items.phrase: without body, parts, or passions

stored_floor_reasons.sonnet: Denying 'parts' entails denial of spatial circumscription, a narrower claim wholly within the immensity floor, though the phrase is primarily about incorporeality/impassibility rather than explicit omnipresence.

items.required_subject_on_card: GOD (the one God, or the Father; not the Church, not humanity, not Christ's human nature)
items.phrase: one only living and true God

items.required_subject_on_card: CHRIST (the two natures of the incarnate Son; the predicate is a delimiter on their union)
items.phrase: there are two natures, the divine and the human, inseparably enjoined in one Person

stored_floor_reasons.sonnet: The passage asserts that the two natures remain distinct ('divine and human') while 'inseparably enjoined in one Person,' which implicitly denies collapse or conversion of one nature into the other, but it never explicitly addresses 'change' or 'conversion'—its explicit emphasis is on inseparability (non-division), not immutability of each nature.

items.required_subject_on_card: CHRIST (the two natures of the incarnate Son; the predicate is a delimiter on their union)
items.phrase: Jesus Christ has both a human and a divine nature

stored_floor_reasons.sonnet: The passage affirms that Christ has both human and divine natures but does not explicitly assert the 'without confusion' concept (non-collapse of distinctions); it only cautions against overemphasizing either side, implying but not stating the predicate directly.

items.required_subject_on_card: GOD AS TRINITY (the predicate delimits how the three persons are described)
items.phrase: in unity of this Godhead there are three persons, of one substance, power, and eternity

stored_floor_reasons.sonnet: The text asserts unity (one substance, power, eternity) and distinction (three persons) simultaneously, which supports but does not explicitly state the negative formula 'neither confounding nor dividing'.

items.required_subject_on_card: GOD (the one God, or the Father; not the Church, not humanity, not Christ's human nature)
items.phrase: in and of himself infinite in being, glory, blessedness, and perfection

stored_floor_reasons.sonnet: Aseity language ('in and of himself infinite in being') entails self-existence and thus indirectly denies creaturehood, but does not explicitly assert 'not made'.
stored_floor_reasons.opus: The passage asserts aseity ("in and of himself") together with eternity and unchangeableness, which entails that God is not made, but it does not in these words explicitly deny creaturehood.

items.required_subject_on_card: GOD (the one God, or the Father; not the Church, not humanity, not Christ's human nature)
items.phrase: one principle of all things, creator of all things invisible and visible

stored_floor_reasons.sonnet: The passage asserts God as sole creator and 'one principle of all things,' which implies supreme originative power but does not explicitly assert governing dominion over creation.

items.required_subject_on_card: GOD (the one God, or the Father; not the Church, not humanity, not Christ's human nature)
items.phrase: The Father incomprehensible, the Son incomprehensible, and the Holy Ghost incomprehensible

stored_floor_reasons.sonnet: Incomprehensibility asserts God's transcendence beyond creaturely understanding, but does not itself state a dissimilarity-exceeds-similarity principle about creaturely likeness to God's mode of being; it is a narrower, related claim.

items.required_subject_on_card: GOD (the one God, or the Father; not the Church, not humanity, not Christ's human nature)
items.phrase: for His own glory

stored_floor_reasons.sonnet: The phrase asserts that glory belongs to God ('His own glory') as the end of His actions, which is narrower than a direct predication that God is glorious as an attribute, but it remains within the floor of glory being properly divine.

items.required_subject_on_card: GOD (the one God, or the Father; not the Church, not humanity, not Christ's human nature)
items.phrase: of His pure unutterable love

stored_floor_reasons.sonnet: The passage asserts that God's love is 'unutterable,' a narrower claim about one divine attribute rather than a general denial that God as such can be exhaustively expressed in language.
stored_floor_reasons.opus: The inexpressibility is predicated of a divine attribute (God's love, the depths of His paternal heart) rather than of the divine essence as such, but it is a narrower proposition lying wholly within the floor of denying exhaustive linguistic expression of God.

items.required_subject_on_card: GOD (the one God, or the Father; not the Church, not humanity, not Christ's human nature)
items.phrase: one eternal, almighty, and incomprehensible God, the Father, Son, and Holy Ghost

stored_floor_reasons.sonnet: The term 'incomprehensible' asserts that God's essence/nature transcends full human comprehension, which overlaps with but is not identical to the specific claim that God's counsel (plans/purposes) resists exhaustive rational penetration; it supports but does not fully specify the defined predicate.

items.required_subject_on_card: CHRIST (the two natures of the incarnate Son; the predicate is a delimiter on their union)
items.phrase: the divine and human natures are perfectly and inseparably united

stored_floor_reasons.sonnet: The passage asserts inseparable union of the two natures, which entails denial of partition into distinct subjects, but uses 'inseparably united' rather than explicit 'without division' language, so it captures the underlying concern narrowly rather than the full Chalcedonian formula.

items.required_subject_on_card: GOD (the one God, or the Father; not the Church, not humanity, not Christ's human nature)
items.phrase: subsisting in himself, all sufficient in himself, invisible, incorporeal, immense, eternal

stored_floor_reasons.sonnet: The passage affirms God as eternal, self-subsisting, and all-sufficient in himself, implying beginninglessness and non-dependence, though it does not explicitly deny a creator or originating act nor state the God-versus-created binary.

items.required_subject_on_card: THE SON (the eternal Son / Logos, as divine)
items.phrase: God from God, Light from Light, true God from true God

stored_floor_reasons.sonnet: The phrase affirms the Son's derivation and consubstantiality with the Father ('Light from Light') which functions as manifestation language, though it emphasizes ontological equality/origin rather than explicit 'image' terminology.

items.required_subject_on_card: GOD (the one God, or the Father; not the Church, not humanity, not Christ's human nature)
items.phrase: righteously opposing all sin and evil

stored_floor_reasons.sonnet: The phrase asserts God's righteous opposition to sin and evil, a narrower relational/active sense rather than a full statement of God's perfect justice as an attribute.
stored_floor_reasons.opus: The standard predicates righteousness of God himself — he acts righteously in opposing all sin and evil — which is the shared divine justice/righteousness the floor requires.

items.required_subject_on_card: THE SON (the eternal Son / Logos, as divine)
items.phrase: In Jesus Christ abide all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge

stored_floor_reasons.sonnet: The text affirms Christ contains wisdom rather than directly naming the Son as 'Wisdom' in the confessional-title sense; it is a related but narrower/adjacent claim about Christ possessing wisdom rather than being identified as Wisdom personified.
stored_floor_reasons.opus: The confession locates all treasures of wisdom in Jesus Christ (echoing Colossians 2:3) rather than explicitly titling the eternal Son 'Wisdom', so it asserts a narrower proposition lying within the predicate's floor.

items.required_subject_on_card: GOD (the one God, or the Father; not the Church, not humanity, not Christ's human nature)
items.phrase: the name of God is in itself holy

stored_floor_reasons.sonnet: The passage affirms holiness of God's name specifically, a narrower but included instance of affirming God's holiness.
stored_floor_reasons.opus: The text affirms intrinsic holiness of God's name rather than predicating holiness of God directly, a narrower proposition that nonetheless falls within the floor since the divine name stands for God Himself as revealed.

items.required_subject_on_card: GOD (the one God, or the Father; not the Church, not humanity, not Christ's human nature)
items.phrase: God patiently preserves humanity and faithfully remains with us even through death

stored_floor_reasons.sonnet: The passage asserts God's steadfast faithfulness and constant presence 'even through death,' which falls within the floor's allowance for covenant faithfulness and constancy of character, though it does not assert strong metaphysical immutability.

items.required_subject_on_card: GOD (the one God, or the Father; not the Church, not humanity, not Christ's human nature)
items.phrase: He works within us to quicken, strengthen and confirm our faith

stored_floor_reasons.sonnet: The passage asserts a narrower proposition—God quickening/strengthening faith via sacramental means—rather than a general theological claim about God's life-giving nature or action.

items.required_subject_on_card: GOD (the one God, or the Father; not the Church, not humanity, not Christ's human nature)
items.phrase: God’s power and goodness are so great and incomprehensible

stored_floor_reasons.sonnet: This asserts incomprehensibility of God's power/goodness regarding providence and theodicy, not a denial of adequate Creator-creature likeness or comparison in general; it is a narrower epistemic claim about divine justice being beyond full human comprehension.
stored_floor_reasons.opus: The passage asserts divine incomprehensibility and that God's works 'surpass human understanding and are beyond our ability to comprehend' — epistemic restraint that entails no adequate human grasp of God, but it stops short of an explicit denial of Creator-creature likeness or comparison.

items.required_subject_on_card: GOD (the one God, or the Father; not the Church, not humanity, not Christ's human nature)
items.phrase: God in his goodness and wisdom reveals himself

stored_floor_reasons.sonnet: Wisdom is attributed to God as a descriptor of the manner of his self-revelation, not asserted as a standalone divine attribute proposition, but it still affirms God's wisdom within the floor.

items.required_subject_on_card: GOD (the one God, or the Father; not the Church, not humanity, not Christ's human nature)
items.phrase: Christ will come in glory and judge the living and the dead

stored_floor_reasons.sonnet: The passage affirms divine judgment but attributes it specifically to Christ (the Son), which is a narrower subject than the required GOD/Father scope.
stored_floor_reasons.opus: It affirms divine eschatological judgment, but predicated of Christ in his coming glory rather than of God simpliciter or the Father, so it is a narrower proposition lying within the floor of shared divine judgment.

items.required_subject_on_card: GOD (the one God, or the Father; not the Church, not humanity, not Christ's human nature)
items.phrase: before whom no God was made or existed, nor shall there be any after Him

stored_floor_reasons.sonnet: The phrase asserts eternal beginninglessness and uniqueness ('no God was made or existed before Him, nor after Him'), which affirms source-status and lack of prior origin, but does not explicitly deny generation of the Son from the Father, so it captures beginninglessness rather than the full 'unbegotten from another' sense.
